statement: Event record names are exactly as written in the issue (ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent, ResourceInstanceCreatedEvent, ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent, ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent) even though existing events are named without the 'Event' suffix (GroupCreated, GroupDeleted).
default_chosen: Names as written in the issue, with the 'Event' suffix
rationale: The owner spelled the names out in the acceptance criteria; tests assert AC text. Renaming later is a mechanical refactor inside Shared.Abstractions and Resources only. Constitution Art. IV example itself uses the suffix (PublishAsync(new SomethingHappenedEvent(...))), so the suffix is not a convention violation.
consequence_if_wrong: Naming inconsistency inside Shared.Abstractions/Events (GroupCreated vs ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent) until someone renames one family.

statement: Deleted-event payloads mirror the created ones: ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent(Guid SchemaId, Guid GroupId) and ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent(Guid ResourceId, Guid SchemaId).
rationale: The issue only names the *Deleted events without payloads; the consumer needs the same keys it stored on creation to remove its rows. GroupId lets Availability clean per-group structures without a lookup.
consequence_if_wrong: If Availability needs more (e.g. DeletedAt), one extra field is added to a record that has no consumer yet — a one-file change.

statement: In CreateResourceTypeRequest and UpdateResourceTypeRequest, BufferMinutes is a non-nullable `int` that binds to 0 when the JSON omits it; on PUT an omitted value therefore resets the buffer to 0 (PUT is already a full replace of Name/Description/PropertyDefinitions).
default_chosen: int BufferMinutes (defaults to 0 when omitted) in both requests
rationale: AC-1: 'defaults to 0 when omitted'. Existing requests are positional records with no optional semantics; a full-replace PUT is the current behaviour for every other field.
consequence_if_wrong: A client that PUTs without BufferMinutes silently drops a previously set buffer. Fix is `int?` + 'keep current when null' in the handler — one file plus one test.
withdrawn_reason: DEC-3: BufferMinutes moved to Availability; out of scope for this story

statement: Validation error message for an out-of-range buffer is 'BufferMinutes must be between 0 and {max}.' via ResourcesDomainException (code = exception type name, as the shared mapper does today).
rationale: Consistent with existing messages ('Resource type name cannot be empty.'); no dedicated exception/409 mapping needed for a plain range violation.
consequence_if_wrong: Message text changes in one handler and one test; frontend does not parse it.
withdrawn_reason: DEC-3: BufferMinutes moved to Availability; out of scope for this story

statement: Integration tests observe published Resources events through a test-side recording decorator of IMessageBroker registered in ThingsBooksyWebAppFactory (captures every IMessage passed to PublishAsync, forwards to the real broker); tests assert the captured event and the persisted row, no consumer module needed.
rationale: F-7: no event sink exists; existing tests prove publication only via consumer side effects, and the consumer (Availability) does not exist. A decorator at the broker is the smallest observable point that is independent of async dispatch timing.
consequence_if_wrong: If the fleet prefers a test-only IEventHandler<T> per event, four small handler classes replace one decorator — test-project-only change.

statement: The two existing integration tests asserting the schema row is hard-deleted (UpdateDeleteResourceTypeTests.cs:185 and :283) are rewritten to assert soft delete (row present with IgnoreQueryFilters, DeletedAt set).

Property definitions of a soft-deleted schema are left untouched (no DeletedAt on ResourcePropertyDefinition); they are hidden together with their schema and would be removed by DB cascade only on a future hard delete.
default_chosen: Leave property definitions as they are
rationale: They are only reachable through the schema (F-2: HasMany PropertyDefinitions with cascade); adding soft delete to them is extra schema work with no observable benefit.
consequence_if_wrong: A later story adds DeletedAt to ResourcePropertyDefinition — separate migration.

statement: Each new event is a public positional record implementing IEvent, one file per record, under Shared.Abstractions/Events/Resources/.

statement: Events are dispatched asynchronously in-process (Channel + AsyncDispatcherJob; outbox disabled) — the story does not enable the outbox; "published after SaveChangesAsync" is satisfied by call order inside the handler.
Deleting an already soft-deleted schema (or instance) is rejected with the existing "not found" domain error (400) and publishes nothing — the load goes through the query filter.
default_chosen: Second delete -> existing not-found error, no event
rationale: Consistent with today's behaviour after a hard delete (row not found); keeps idempotency on the consumer side trivial (no duplicate Deleted events).
consequence_if_wrong: If a 204 idempotent delete is preferred, one branch in each delete handler.
